text: If you only listen to what women say, dating will often feel confusing. Because many things are communicated indirectly. The real message is usually in the behavior, not just in words. In this series, we go through common phrases women say, what they often mean in reality, and how you should react if you want to keep your self-respect. Imagine you are texting with a girl you know from school or from some activity that you both do. You like her, and logically, you ask her out. But she hits you with, sorry, I'm not ready for dating right now. Bad news, bye, the translation here is, I don't like you enough to go on a date with you. But I'm a nice person, so I don't want to say it directly to your face. And if another guy, a guy I actually like, asks me out, then suddenly, I might be ready for dating. Now, the good news is that there is a small trick you can try. You can say something like, look, I'm not talking about dating, I'm not ready for dating myself. I just want to meet and get to know you better, like an interesting person. That's it. If she then agrees to meet you, you still have a chance if you act right on a date. But even if after that she still doesn't agree, it's fine. Just say thank you, wish her a good day, and move on. Now, let's look at a different variation. Let's say there's a more positive scenario. You are already seeing a girl casually. In other words, you are in a situation. Things are going well, so you decide to take it to the next step. You ask her if she wants to move into a more serious, exclusive phase. But she tells you, you know, I'm not ready for something serious right now. The translation here is this. I'm not ready for something serious with you right now. You are nice to spend some time with when I'm bored or when I have free time, but you don't fit my criteria for a serious partner. If there will be a guy who fits my criteria, I will suddenly be ready for a serious relationship. In this situation, I would say the best course of action is to end even the casual thing with her. Another important point. As a man, I don't recommend that you push the serious relationship conversation yourself. In most cases, it should be initiated by the woman. Yes, in a way, it is an interesting double standard. As a man, you are expected to initiate the process, introduce yourself, ask the girl out, plan the date, do the whole courting thing. But once you actually start seeing each other, the move towards something serious should come from her side. And that gives you an important advantage. It gives you time to observe her behavior and decide for yourself whether you even want something serious with her. And if the girl is not initiating anything serious after, let's say, two or three months of seeing each other, that is already your answer. You don't even need to ask the question. Her actions have already told you everything you needed to know.
